Question: By inserting parentheses, it is possible to give the expression \[2 \times 3 + 4 \times 5\] several values. How many different values can be obtained?
Solution:
Parentheses change the order of calculation while keeping the numbers and operation signs in their original order. Any partially parenthesized expression can be fully parenthesized without changing its value, so it suffices to list the full groupings.

Organize them by the operation performed last. If the first multiplication is last, there are two ways to group the expression to its right. If the addition is last, there is one possibility. If the last multiplication is last, there are two ways to group the expression to its left. This gives the complete list:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2\times(3+(4\times5))&=46,\\
2\times((3+4)\times5)&=70,\\
(2\times3)+(4\times5)&=26,\\
((2\times3)+4)\times5&=50,\\
(2\times(3+4))\times5&=70.
\end{aligned}
\]
We count values, so the repeated value \(70\) is counted only once. The distinct values are \(26,46,50,70\), giving \(\boxed{4}\), choice C.
